en: At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
On that occasion, the Blessed One was sitting reflecting on his own abandonment of the tendency toward conceptual proliferation (*papañca-saññā-saṅkhā*).
Then, having understood his own abandonment of the tendency toward conceptual proliferation, at that time the Blessed One uttered this inspired exclamation (*udāna*):
“He for whom there is no proliferation, nor any persistence,
who has transcended the bond and the crossbar—
that sage wandering free from craving— ”
“Even the world with its gods does not despise him.
